evidenceAudit.scope: Asymptomatic adults (and at-risk adolescents): who to screen for prediabetes and type 2 diabetes, tests and thresholds, repeat intervals and prevention for prediabetes. Verified against the Saudi Diabetes Clinical Practice Guidelines (SDCPG 2021, pp. 19–22) and the Saudi PHA Clinical Preventive Guideline 2023.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 12 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: HbA1c reliability in haemoglobinopathies (common in KSA) not addressed in source

pathophysiology.summary: Type 2 diabetes develops over years through insulin resistance and progressive beta-cell failure, passing through prediabetes. Saudi Arabia has a high prevalence from age 35, so screening detects disease early when lifestyle change and treatment prevent complications (SDCPG).
keyMechanisms: Insulin resistance (obesity, inactivity) precedes hyperglycaemia; prediabetes reflects early beta-cell strain.
HbA1c reflects average glucose over about 3 months.
Intensive lifestyle change and metformin delay progression from prediabetes (SDCPG).

symptoms: Risk factors: family history, previous GDM, PCOS, hypertension, dyslipidaemia, physical inactivity.
physicalSigns: BMI 25 or more; waist 102 cm or more (men) or 88 cm or more (women) (SDCPG); acanthosis nigricans.
redFlags: Glucose 11.1 mmol/L or more with symptoms — diagnose and treat

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Young, lean, ketosis — no routine screening (SDCPG).

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Diabetes: HbA1c 6.5% or more; fasting 7.0 mmol/L (126 mg/dL) or more; 2-h OGTT 11.1 mmol/L (200 mg/dL) or more. Prediabetes: HbA1c 5.7–6.4%; fasting 5.6–6.9 mmol/L (100–125 mg/dL); 2-h 7.8–11.0 mmol/L (140–199 mg/dL).
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Without symptoms, confirm with a second abnormal test (SDCPG).
ruleIn.normalValue: HbA1c below 5.7%; fasting below 5.6 mmol/L (100 mg/dL)

clinicalManagement.title: Who to screen (SDCPG)
actions: Earlier if BMI 25 or more (or abdominal obesity) plus 1 or more risk factor: first-degree relative with diabetes, previous GDM, CVD, hypertension (140/90 or treated), HDL below 0.90 or TG above 2.82 mmol/L, smoking, pancreatitis, gout, fatty liver, psychiatric illness, HIV, sleep apnoea, PCOS, macrosomic baby, inactivity, diabetogenic drugs.
Adolescents after age 10 or puberty if overweight/obese with 1 or more risk factor.

clinicalManagement.title: Repeat interval
actions: Normal: repeat at least every 3 years (yearly if high risk) (SDCPG).
Prediabetes: test yearly. Previous GDM: lifelong testing at least every 3 years.

clinicalManagement.title: Prediabetes
actions: Intensive lifestyle programme aiming for 7% weight loss and 150 min/week moderate activity (SDCPG).
Metformin for prediabetes with BMI 35 or more, previous GDM, or age under 60: 500 mg once daily, increasing to 1,500–2,000 mg/day (SDCPG).
Screen and manage CVD risk factors (SDCPG).

learningObjectives: Screen at-risk adults for prediabetes and type 2 diabetes and prevent progression.

keyPoints: Earlier if overweight with a risk factor.
Confirm with a second test if asymptomatic.
pitfalls: Using HbA1c when it is unreliable (anaemia, haemoglobinopathy).

patientEducation: Lifestyle change prevents or delays diabetes.
lifestyleAndDiet: Mediterranean, low-calorie or low-fat eating plan; reduce sugary drinks; 150 min/week activity (SDCPG).
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Prediabetes: glucose or HbA1c every 3–6 months on metformin, at least yearly otherwise (SDCPG).

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: BMI 25 or more plus 1 risk factor

regimens.indication: Prediabetes with BMI 35 or more, prior GDM, or age under 60
regimens.dose: 500 mg once daily, increasing as tolerated
regimens.frequency: Once to twice daily with meals
regimens.duration: Target 1,500–2,000 mg/day; long term with review
adjustments: Do not start if eGFR 30–45; stop if below 30 (label)
